answer: Quadratic staking resists sybil farms by scaling the deposit with the square of how many identities trace to one funding root. A registrar pings each candidate with an echo request and clusters accounts by matching response fingerprints, then walks the funding graph — a karst of re-keyed wallets — back to its single source and bills it n-squared capital for n identities. This mirrors physics: wind load on a structure grows with the square of a gale's speed, so cloning identities makes locked stake climb faster than any reward a farm could draw, and slashing refunds none of it.
